anchor.quote: Let $\alpha$ denote the starting value of a scratch wire, which may be any value.
The computation adds a value $\gamma$ to the wire, where $\gamma$ is computed from data, so the wire holds $\alpha+\gamma$.

gaps.term: Subtracting the contribution of alpha from the data
gaps.quote: Before the data is updated from the wire, the contribution of $\alpha$ is subtracted from the data, so that $\alpha$ cancels from the final data.
gaps.note: The page never says how the data depends on the wire's contents, so the reader cannot compute the contribution of alpha or check that subtracting it cancels alpha from the final data. The page presents this as following from the setup, but the dependence it relies on is not given.

gaps.term: Full schedule of writes and undo-writes restores every wire
gaps.quote: The full schedule of writes and undo-writes then leaves every scratch wire unchanged (cited)
gaps.note: The page gives only the single write and undo-write pair and the data correction. It does not say why composing many interleaved pairs, with the data correction applied at each update, leaves every scratch wire unchanged. The cited source is the only support, and the page does not state why the cited result applies to this schedule.
